status: Integrated source-fit matter programme; retained historical specific judgments remain separately identified, not upgraded from link counts.

definition-and-change.readScope: Actual main physical/chemical definition and ordinary change examples read; no figures visually checked or advanced intensive/extensive/hazard/periodic-table sections adopted.
definition-and-change.treatment: Factual reference only; no textbook wording, images, activities or assessment copied. Current licence restrictions are not represented as a general permission to redistribute.

properties.task: Use ordinary water, an opaque block and contained air; distinguish matter from emitted light with both mass and occupied-space reasons. Compare actual solid/liquid/gas behaviour, including the retained eight-plus state classification and tricky sand/vapour/droplet cases. Test selected relevant material properties and give a reasoned use from the preceding reviewed property programme.
properties.evidence: Names specific observed/provided properties, separates a measured result from a supplied fact and explains what each supports; an unseen gas is not nothing.

state-change.task: Use the reviewed actual melting-water observation and the provided colder-freezer account. Identify substance/state before and after, name the direction of thermal transfer for the chosen material and surroundings, then explain a condensation example from home or community. Retain appropriate actual Celsius observations and ordinary-pressure reference conditions where testing the whole existing heating/cooling claim.
state-change.evidence: The water remains water across state changes; thermal energy enters during melting and leaves during freezing. Temperature alone is not the amount or direction of transferred energy.

physical-change.task: Actually reshape safe modelling clay and contrast spring-back versus retained deformation using the existing material bench. Separately dissolve ordinary salt in water and use a prepared recovered-salt example or adult-managed evaporation. Explain what changed and what remained the same; water need not be recovered in an open dish.
physical-change.evidence: Shape/state/physical form can change without a new substance. Explain the specific recovery operation for the selected recoverable examples, while a torn or crushed physical object need not be easy to restore exactly.
physical-change.limits: Whole reversible-change evidence retains at least three appropriate do-and-undo examples. Practical recovery is related to chemical identity but is not its universal definition.

chemical-change.task: Use a small open-container adult-supervised vinegar/bicarbonate observation, an attributed rusting-iron account and a supplied cooked/burnt-food account. Record actual evidence versus provided account, identify a new substance and compare with boiling/condensing water, dissolving salt and an opened fizzy drink. No pupil burning, gas trapping in rigid sealed vessels or tasting unknown mixtures.
chemical-change.evidence: New substances distinguish the chemical cases; a change in colour, gas or temperature may be a clue rather than proof by itself. Existing gas escaping from a drink and state-change bubbles are near misses. Simple cooling/sieving does not restore the selected reacted materials.
chemical-change.limits: No assertion that every chemical process is absolutely irreversible, every physical change is easy to undo or every reaction emits heat. No new reversible-reaction/equation inventory is required.

preparation: Retain the three preceding reviewed matter/state/property dossiers and their actual supplied facts; prepare unfilled observations/reasoning records and ordinary safe materials. Data are recorded only when observed, never copied from an invented expected result.
Prepare the original four integrated case briefs. Use the same before/change/after/evidence/reason format so the learner must discriminate transformations rather than memorise a label.
learnerActions: Complete all four case areas and explain the relationship between a material property, its state under stated conditions, and the kind of change observed.

For the physical and chemical comparison, identify the starting and resulting material, cite evidence and explain why heat, bubbles, appearance or difficulty undoing alone is not a sufficient category rule.
Compare the two heated cases: melting water and a supplied cooked-food change. Explain why heating occurs in both but only the latter selected case forms new substances.

Transfer to two original changed briefs: a sheet is torn into pieces; a cold bottle gains droplets outside. Explain whether new substances are established, what evidence supports the answer and what is not yet known.
successEvidence: Actual integrated before/after/reasoned account across all four required areas, retaining the specific task performances rather than only reading their reports.
Specific state/property/change distinctions and correctly qualified recovery reasoning; no copied labels, fabricated observations or thermal/chemical universal rules.
nearMisses: Names all three states but treats the gas as nothing or fails to account for the actual occupied-space criterion.
Calls every heated/bubbling event chemical or every hard-to-undo physical break a new substance.
Treats three completed source associations or a supplied reaction animation as proof that the learner performed every whole claim.
protocol.transfer: Explain the torn-paper and cold-bottle cases, then choose one new material-use brief from the property dossier with a reason supported by the available observations.

wholeClaimBoundary.review: Complete cards and full guides for state classification, heating/cooling, reshaping, reversible/irreversible changes and material properties read; direct readiness cards/edges reviewed. Dissolving whole card and assessment also read.
wholeClaimBoundary.retained: Whole states includes eight-plus/tricky classifications; whole heating includes actual observation/Celsius conditions; whole reshaping includes all four actions; whole recoverable-change task includes actual do-and-undo cases. No limited overall probe certifies all those mastery states.
wholeClaimBoundary.inheritedQualityIssue: Some inherited reversible/irreversible guidance uses absolute recoverability language. This accurate source-specific programme distinguishes chemical identity from ordinary practical reversal; a separate exact factual-correction proposal is pending. Existing historical metadata/claims/guides are unchanged here.
wholeClaimBoundary.readiness: Existing hard particle/heating/state/property/dissolving paths remain recorded and separately assessed. No prerequisite waiver, age lowering, or inferred mastery is made.

canonicalChanges: Add the overall source component key to the six existing Ontario10–11 contexts only; no topic, authored claim, guide, interval or dependency change.
coverageBoundary: Source-fit authoring coverage, not recorded learner success, acceptance on default main, or staging publication. The nine historical specific Full judgments remain historical; this integrated programme is independently designed for the overall duty.
